text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Autonomic dysreflexia: a written plan and wallet card (sit him up, loosen clothing, check the catheter and bladder, then the bowel and skin; check blood pressure every 2 to 5 minutes; nitroglycerin ointment only if systolic pressure stays at 150 mmHg or higher), his baseline blood pressure recorded, and training for every nurse
  • Physical medicine and rehabilitation (spinal cord injury medicine) consultation to review the pacer conditioning plan, the autonomic dysreflexia plan, bladder and bowel management, bone health, spasticity and pain, and seating and equipment
  • Pressure injury prevention: skin checks morning and night by his nurses, tilt-in-space pressure relief every 30 minutes in the chair, turning every 2 hours in bed on a pressure-redistributing mattress, cushion and seating review, nutrition, and the Braden scale at each visit
  • Neurogenic bladder: catheter care with monthly changes and closed drainage, no treatment of bacteria in the urine without symptoms, kidney function by cystatin C, and kidney and bladder ultrasound yearly
  • Neurogenic bowel: a daily morning program with a suppository and digital stimulation, senna at night, fiber and fluids, reviewed at each visit
  • Respiratory care: tracheostomy care, suctioning, daily mechanical insufflation-exsufflation for secretion clearance, a pacer conditioning schedule with oxygen saturation checks, a backup ventilator, a spare tracheostomy tube, a generator and battery plan for power cuts, and registration with the power company and emergency services
  • Bone health and cardiometabolic risk: calcium, 25-hydroxyvitamin D and PTH, DXA of the hip and knee regions, continued electrically stimulated cycling, careful transfers; lipids, A1c and blood pressure yearly
  • Mood, pain, spasticity and venous thromboembolism: PHQ-9 at intake and twice a year, pain score at reviews, stretching and range of motion for spasticity, and checking for leg swelling, with urgent assessment for a new swollen leg
  • On the consultant's advice: vitamin D3 1977 units daily with a recheck in about eight weeks, seating pressure mapping with a cushion review, a weekly step-up of pacer time as tolerated, and a repeat DXA in two years

resource.title: Christopher Reeve synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care, coordinated with spinal cord injury medicine, for a 50-year-old director and advocate living with chronic incomplete C2 tetraplegia, ventilator use through a tracheostomy and a newly implanted diaphragm pacing system, on the Paralyzed Veterans of America Consortium for Spinal Cord Medicine guidelines: recognizing autonomic dysreflexia and keeping a written plan with him and his nurses, pressure injury prevention with daily skin checks and the Braden scale, neurogenic bladder care with kidney surveillance by cystatin C and ultrasound, a daily bowel program, respiratory care with secretion clearance and a pacer conditioning schedule, vaccinations, venous thromboembolism awareness, bone health with DXA and vitamin D, spasticity and pain, cardiometabolic risk, mood screening, care team and equipment needs including power and ventilator backup, and advance care planning, with disability presented as part of a full working life.
